intro: On 1 March 2021 somebody took a knife to this tamarind's roots trying to kill it. Nine months later Piauí made it a heritage site, banning anyone from pruning, mutilating, felling or disturbing it again. What draws visitors is the crown: constant onshore wind has swept the whole canopy hard to one side, like hair combed in a single stroke, which gives the tree its name, Árvore Penteada, the combed tree. It stands beside the PI-116 highway near Praia do Arrombado, reached by car or moto-taxi.

question_answer: Luís Correia's notable tree is the Árvore Penteada (the combed tree), a Tamarind swept sideways by onshore wind, beside the PI-116 highway near Praia do Arrombado, a Piauí state Historic and Environmental Heritage site since December 2021.
question_context: The tree survived a deliberate attack: on 1 March 2021 somebody cut several of its roots with a large knife, investigated by the state environmental agency Semar and the police as an environmental crime. Nine months later, on 23 December 2021, the state legislature passed Law 7.688, declaring the tree Historic and Environmental Heritage and banning anyone from pruning, mutilating, removing, felling or disturbing it, exactly where the knife went in. What draws most visitors is its shape rather than its history: constant onshore wind has pushed the whole crown hard to one side, as though combed in a single stroke, which is where the local name comes from. A folk legend, told by writer Tharlliton Silva, offers a different explanation, that a woman named Francisca Penteada was turned into the tree by jealous rivals; that is folklore, and the wind is the better-documented story. Residents put its age at over 70 years. It stands within 250 metres of the PI-116 highway near the turning for Praia do Arrombado, a roadside stop that gained visitor facilities after the 2021 listing.

trees.story:
On 1 March 2021 somebody took a large knife to this tamarind's roots and tried to kill it. Nine months later the state of Piauí made it a heritage site.

The tree survived the attack. The state environmental agency, Semar, and the police investigated it as an environmental crime, and on 23 December 2021 the state legislature passed Law 7.688, declaring the tree Historic and Environmental Heritage. The law bans pruning it, mutilating it, removing it, felling it, or disturbing the ground around it, which is exactly where the knife went in.

What people come for is the crown. The onshore wind that blows constantly along this coast has pushed all of it hard to one side, like hair combed in a single stroke, which is where the name comes from: Árvore Penteada, the combed tree. A local legend, told by the writer Tharlliton Silva, explains it differently: a woman called Francisca Penteada, turned into a tree by jealous rivals. That is folklore, and the wind is the better story anyway.

Residents put its age at over 70 years, and nobody has published anything more exact, nor a measurement of the trunk. If you have one, tell us.

It stands within 250 metres of the PI-116 coastal highway near the turning for Praia do Arrombado and Carnaubinha, a roadside stop that gained basic visitor facilities after the listing. It was still drawing visitors in 2023. There is no bus; come by car or moto-taxi from Luís Correia or Parnaíba.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the crown, a tamarind's whole canopy swept hard to one side by the wind. It stands within 250 metres of the PI-116 near the Praia do Arrombado and Carnaubinha turning, at the roadside visitor stop.
